title: Lab 6 — Quiz 2
subtitle: Survey of Eukaryotes — helminths and comparisons

questions.prompt: Identify this structure, used by a tapeworm to attach to the intestinal wall.
questions.explanation: Taenia uses its scolex, with hooks and suction cups, to attach to the intestinal wall. (Viewed with the 10X lens in lab.)

why.A: Ascaris ova are wide oval eggs.
why.B: Enterobius ova are flat oval eggs.
why.D: Aspergillus is a fungus with dandelion-shaped heads.

questions.prompt: This long, flat, segmented worm is Taenia. What type of helminth is it?
questions.explanation: Taenia spp. are cestodes — common intestinal tapeworms of animals and people.

why.A: Ascaris and Enterobius are the nematodes.
why.C: Helminths are multicellular animals, not protozoa.

questions.prompt: How do pets most often get tapeworms?

options.text: By eating Ascaris eggs from soil
By drinking water with Giardia cysts

questions.explanation: Pets most often get tapeworms by swallowing larvae-infected fleas. Humans may swallow egg sacs or larvae in contaminated water, or larvae in undercooked meat.

why.A: Ascaris is a roundworm, not a tapeworm.

questions.prompt: Identify these eggs: wide, oval-shaped ova with a thick, bumpy shell.

why.A: Enterobius ova are flat and oval.
why.B: Entamoeba cysts are protozoan cysts, not helminth eggs.
why.C: The scolex is the tapeworm's attachment structure.

questions.prompt: Identify these eggs: flat, oval-shaped ova.

why.A: Ascaris ova are wide and oval.
why.B: Yeast cells are much smaller and bud.

questions.prompt: Which helminth is very common in the US (especially in children), and its females exit the anus to lay eggs, causing intense itching?
questions.explanation: Enterobius: intestinal pinworm; fecal-oral; females exit the anus and lay eggs on the skin, causing intense itching.

why.B: Ascaris is common worldwide but less so in the US.
why.C: Taenia attaches to the intestinal wall by its scolex.

questions.prompt: These intestinal roundworms can interfere with breathing and may cause intestinal blockage. Identify them.
questions.explanation: Ascaris: nematode; very common worldwide; eggs ingested, hatch in the small intestine; can interfere with breathing and cause intestinal blockage.

options.text: Nematodes spread by the fecal-oral route

questions.explanation: Both are nematodes: eggs are ingested (fecal-oral) and hatch in the intestines.

why.B: Neither is a trematode or mosquito-borne.

questions.prompt: Which protozoan has ONLY a trophozoite form (no cysts)?
questions.explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis only has a trophozoite form.

why.D: Naegleria's figure shows a cyst stage too.

questions.prompt: This round structure is an Entamoeba histolytica cyst. Which other protozoan from lab also forms cysts and trophozoites?
questions.explanation: Both Entamoeba histolytica and Giardia lamblia form cysts and trophozoites and spread by the fecal-oral route.

why.A: Trichomonas only has a trophozoite form.
why.B: Plasmodium is described as an intracellular parasite in RBCs.
why.D: Amoeba proteus isn't described as forming cysts in the slides.

questions.prompt: Which lens is used to view the Taenia scolex slide in the microscopic survey?
questions.explanation: Survey: 40X for Aspergillus, Penicillium, Amoeba proteus and Ascaris ova; 10X for the Taenia scolex.

why.A: Aspergillus, Penicillium, Amoeba and Ascaris ova are viewed at 40X.
why.C: The manual specifies 10X for the scolex.

questions.prompt: Compared with prokaryotes, eukaryotic cells are:

options.text: 1–10 µm with a nucleus and organelles
10–100 µm with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles

questions.explanation: Prokaryotes: 1–10 µm, no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. Eukaryotes: 10–100 µm, nucleus and organelles, compartmentalized.

why.A: 1–10 µm is the prokaryote size range.

questions.prompt: Fungal culture: which genus is shown growing as this colony?
questions.explanation: The slide shows Aspergillus in culture, in brightfield and by SEM.

questions.prompt: These SEM images show protozoa lining an intestinal surface. Identify them.
questions.explanation: Giardia trophozoites attach to the intestine; they cause fatty diarrhea.

why.C: Plasmodium lives inside red blood cells.
why.D: Amoeba proteus is free-living and non-pathogenic.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Penicillium is FALSE?

options.text: Its spore-forming structures look like brooms

questions.explanation: Penicillium is NOT known to cause disease. Aspergillus is the one that causes respiratory problems (farmer's lung, aspergillosis).
